The polar scope incorporates an optical lens (11) and an image sensor (12) configured to capture constellation images (IM). After receiving these images from the polar scope, the controller identifies both the polar-axis rotation-center position (P1) and the celestial-pole position (P2). The polar axis calibration system comprises a polar scope, a calibration control device, and a display device. The polar scope includes an optical lens and an image sensor configured to capture images of constellations in the region of the celestial pole. These images are transmitted to the calibration control device for processing.

Using the captured constellation image, the calibration control device determines both the rotation center of the polar axis and the position of the celestial pole. The display device then presents the constellation image together with visual indicators showing the identified celestial pole position and the polar axis rotation center.

During calibration, the user adjusts the polar axis until its rotation center is directly aligned with the celestial pole indicated on the display. This image-based alignment method improves calibration accuracy while reducing the installation-precision requirements of the polar scope. As a result, the system provides a more reliable and convenient approach to polar axis calibration.
outputs.L4:
A polar-axis calibration system is provided for accurately aligning the polar axis of an astronomical mount with a celestial pole. The system includes a polar scope equipped with an optical sensor and an image sensor. The optical sensor detects the rotational position or movement of the polar axis, while the image sensor captures images of a region of the sky containing recognizable stars or constellations. A control device receives data from both sensors and processes a plurality of captured constellation images to determine the rotation center corresponding to the polar axis. The control device also analyzes the star patterns in the images to identify the position of the relevant celestial pole.

The determined polar-axis rotation center and celestial-pole position are presented on a display, preferably as marks, symbols, or other indicators superimposed on a live or recorded image of the sky. A user can then adjust the orientation of the astronomical mount until the displayed rotation center substantially coincides with the displayed celestial-pole position. In some implementations, the system may additionally provide directional prompts, offset values, or real-time feedback during adjustment.

Because calibration is performed by directly aligning the calculated rotation center with the detected celestial pole, the polar scope does not need to be installed with extremely high mechanical precision relative to the mount. Errors caused by assembly tolerances, optical-axis offsets, or slight misalignment of the scope can be compensated for through image processing and positional calculation. The system therefore improves polar-alignment accuracy, simplifies installation and calibration, and enables reliable alignment even when the polar scope itself is not perfectly centered or oriented.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a polar axis calibration system that uses a polar scope, image sensor, control device, and display to align an equatorial mount’s polar-axis rotation center with the celestial pole.
counterfactuals.output: A polar-axis calibration system for an equatorial mount includes a polar scope aligned with a polar axis of the mount, an image sensor configured to capture images of a celestial field through the polar scope, a control device, and a display. The control device processes one or more captured images to identify celestial reference objects and determine a position of a celestial pole within an image coordinate system. The control device further determines a rotation center of the polar axis from image data acquired at different rotational positions of the equatorial mount, compares the rotation center with the determined position of the celestial pole, and generates alignment information representing a direction and magnitude of polar-axis adjustment. The display presents the captured celestial field and a visual indication of the alignment information to guide adjustment of the equatorial mount until the rotation center substantially coincides with the celestial pole.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into patent-style language: a camera-equipped polar scope captures star-field images, a controller identifies the mount’s rotation center and the celestial pole in the image plane, and a display shows both positions so the user can align them directly.
counterfactuals.output:
### Patent-Style Description

A polar-alignment apparatus for an astronomical mount comprises an imaging device optically coupled to a polar scope and configured to capture one or more images of a stellar field. A controller processes the captured images to determine, in an image coordinate system, a first position corresponding to a rotational center of the astronomical mount and a second position corresponding to a celestial pole. A display presents respective visual indicators representing the first and second positions, thereby enabling a user to adjust the astronomical mount until the visual indicators substantially coincide.

### Exemplary Independent Claim

1. **A polar-alignment system for an astronomical mount, comprising:**
   
   an imaging device configured to capture at least one image of a star field through a polar scope associated with the astronomical mount;
   
   a controller configured to:
   
   identify, within an image plane of the imaging device, a rotational-center position corresponding to an axis of rotation of the astronomical mount; and
   
   determine, within the image plane, a celestial-pole position corresponding to a celestial pole; and
   
   a display configured to concurrently present a first indicator representing the rotational-center position and a second indicator representing the celestial-pole position, such that alignment of the astronomical mount is facilitated by adjustment of the mount to bring the first indicator and the second indicator into substantial coincidence.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Prepare an English patent abstract for a polar scope calibration invention, referencing a polar axis calibration system (100), polar scope (10), control device (20), display device (30), equatorial instrument (500), and polar axis (510).
counterfactuals.output: A polar axis calibration system (100) for calibrating a polar scope (10) mounted on an equatorial instrument (500) is disclosed. The system (100) includes a control device (20) configured to acquire polar-scope observation data at a plurality of rotational positions of a polar axis (510), determine a reference position corresponding to the polar axis (510), and calculate a calibration deviation of the polar scope (10) relative to the reference position. A display device (30) is configured to display calibration information representing the calculated deviation and/or an adjustment instruction for correcting the orientation or indicated center of the polar scope (10). By determining the calibration deviation during rotation of the polar axis (510), the system (100) enables accurate alignment of the equatorial instrument (500) with a celestial pole and reduces errors caused by mechanical or optical offset of the polar scope (10).
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a patent disclosure covering a polar scope, a polar-axis calibration controller, an equatorial mount, and an astronomical telescope, emphasizing image-based pole alignment, direct matching of the celestial pole to the mechanical rotation center, and tolerance for polar-scope installation error.
counterfactuals.output:
The disclosure describes a polar-alignment system for an equatorial telescope mount that uses images captured through a polar scope rather than relying on precise mechanical installation or a fixed reticle.

A controller acquires polar-scope images containing stars near the celestial pole, identifies the star field, and determines the celestial-pole position from astronomical data. By comparing images taken at different rotational positions of the mount’s polar/right-ascension axis, it also calculates the axis’s actual mechanical rotation center in the image. The system then provides guidance—or controls mount adjustment—so that the detected celestial pole is brought directly into coincidence with that rotation center.

Because alignment is based on the measured rotation center rather than an assumed polar-scope optical axis or reticle center, offsets, tilt, and other polar-scope installation errors have little effect on accuracy. The disclosure applies this approach to the polar scope and its calibration controller, to an equatorial mount incorporating them, and to an astronomical telescope equipped with the mount.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
